text: Food safety requires heating components for specific durations until safe to eat. Simmering entails keeping items submerged in water or stock at a low heat, which softens them and builds complexity. This approach yields deep tastes and soft consistencies, making it ideal for stocks, gravies, and stews. Conversely, seasoning applies salts, peppercorns, herbs, and spices to modify flavor profiles. Proper application of this step improves the final taste. Combining these distinct methods successfully produces a superior dish.
